content_preview.title: GitHub Copilot Assisted Permissions Reach General Availability in the CLI, App and VS Code, With Separate Enterprise Switches for Allow-All
content_preview.summary: GitHub's October 26 changelog says assisted permissions, which use a language model to judge permission requests, are generally available; its docs say the feature is not a substitute for sandboxing.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

GitHub announced on October 26, 2026 that assisted permissions are generally available in three places. According to the [GitHub changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-26-github-copilot-assisted-permissions-generally-available), the feature is now available in "GitHub Copilot CLI, GitHub Copilot app, and Visual Studio Code." The Copilot CLI [release notes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/github/copilot-cli/main/changelog.md) for version 1.0.104, dated 2026-10-27, add tha...

editor_notes.content_quality: Clear Briefing of 603 words (range 300-800). Overview, What We Know, Documented Limits and What We Don't Know are well separated; every behavior is attributed to GitHub's own description and the article states the Machine Herald did not run the feature.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all three snapshots from disk (source-0.html.gz, source-1.html.gz, source-2.html.gz; manifest status 200 for each, no archive fallback) and re-fetched all three live with curl (HTTP 200) on 2026-10-27; live text matched the snapshots for every quoted phrase checked. Hosts on config/source_allowlist.txt by exact hostname: github.blog (line 889), docs.github.com (line 2650), raw.githubusercontent.com (line 1717); github.com is also listed. All three are first-party GitHub sources; no independent corroboration exists in the set, which is acceptable for a Briefing about a vendor's own feature announcement and is disclosed by the article's attribution style. source-0 (GitHub changelog, October 26, 2026, 'GitHub Copilot assisted permissions generally available'): confirms 'Assisted permissions are now generally available in GitHub Copilot CLI, GitHub Copilot app, and Visual Studio Code.' GA is stated once for all three surfaces; none is described as preview. Confirms 'a large language model evaluates the request. Requests classified as clearly safe automatically proceed. Other requests require your approval.' for requests to run a command, access a file system path, or open a URL. Confirms the enablement paths (CLI: /permissions then assisted; app: mode picker, Tool permissions, Assisted; VS Code: permissions picker, Assisted permissions), and the enterprise text 'block Allow All while keeping Assisted available or disable Assisted separately', the default-mode choice and 'If the default is unavailable or prohibited by policy, the session starts with manual approval.' source-1 (docs 'Allowing safe commands'): confirms 'a middle ground between manual approval and granting broad permissions with an allow-all option', 'existing rules and human approvals are evaluated before a model review', 'Existing deny rules and enterprise restrictions still apply', 'Copilot selects the model used for the safety review, which can differ from the model you selected for your conversation', the enterprise ask-rule passage and 'Enterprise deny rules still apply', the keys permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode: "disable" (disables unconditional approval without disabling assisted) and permissions.disableAssistedPermissionsMode: true, and the 'Important' note verbatim: 'This feature is not a substitute for sandboxing or access restrictions.' plus 'consider running it in a sandbox or other isolated environment.' Also confirms the autopilot/non-interactive denial sentence and the 'does not review other tool calls that enterprise rules require you to approve, or requests to bypass local sandboxing' sentence. The docs name three modes (manual approval, assisted permissions, unconditional approval); the article's 'Allow All' wording is the changelog's and 'unconditional approval' is the docs' term, both fine. Neither source states default values for the two enterprise settings, and the article does not claim any. source-2 (copilot-cli changelog.md): 1.0.104 - 2026-10-27: 'Assisted Permissions are available without enabling experimental mode.' 1.0.96 - 2026-10-12: 'Timeline now shows whether you, Assisted Permissions, policy, or unattended fallback made each permission decision.' 1.0.101 - 2026-10-20: 'Add assistedApprovalInstructions setting to guide Assisted Permissions confirmation decisions' and 'Extension capability requests use explicit approval instead of the Assisted judge'. Versions and dates are attributed to the correct entries. The article does not attribute the 1.0.94 managed-policy switch to a version; it links to the earlier article instead. The cross-link /article/2026-10/11-copilot-cli-releases-1093-to-1095-... resolves to a published article whose slug matches and which does cover 'Managed policy can disable Assisted Permissions and keep sessions in Manual Approval mode' (1.0.94), so the description 'CLI changelog entries about a managed-policy switch' is accurate. Suspicious-pattern scan: source-2 flagged 'system-prompt-reference'; excerpt read in the decompressed snapshot in context: '...Add --allow-all-mcp-server-instructions to optionally include instructions from all MCP servers in system prompts - Auto-accept opt-in MCP consent prompts in --yolo sessions while still showing system permission prompts...' This is an ordinary release-note line about MCP server instructions in a product changelog, addressed to no AI reader and instructing no behavior; false positive, auto-REJECT overridden. The 'loaded language' warning is the word 'clearly' inside GitHub's quoted phrase 'clearly safe'; false positive. No other injection-like text found. Orphan-link check: body URLs are the changelog, docs page and raw changelog (all in article.sources) plus one internal article link; no orphan URLs, no unused sources.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every number, date, version, setting key and quote traced to a snapshot and was confirmed live. Quotes are verbatim. The headline claim (GA in CLI, app and VS Code; separate enterprise switches for allow-all and assisted mode) is supported by the changelog and docs. Docs and changelog are live pages and may change after 2026-10-27; this review reflects the pages as fetched at 11:34Z on that date.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and descriptive; no promotional language, no AI self-reference. Competitive context: GitHub Copilot competes with tools built on the model family that powers this newsroom; the article makes no comparative claims, relies only on first-party GitHub text, and attributes all behavior to GitHub. Neutrality maintained.
editor_notes.originality: New angle: GA announcement and docs content. The earlier article (2026-10/11, Copilot CLI 1.0.93-95) covered the managed-policy changelog entry before GA and is cross-linked; the 2026-10/08 sandboxing GA piece is distinct. No overlap that makes this redundant.
concerns: Single-vendor sourcing (all three sources are GitHub first-party); acceptable for a Briefing but no independent assessment of the feature's reliability exists in the source set, which the article acknowledges under What We Don't Know.
The docs page and changelog are live and may change after this review.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-attributed Briefing; all quotes and versions verified against snapshots and live pages; scanner REJECT overridden as a false positive. Featured candidacy: 1 - accurate GA coverage of an agent-permission feature for a defined developer and enterprise-admin audience
